title: RFID Solution Provider — Tags, Cards, Encoding & Integration Support
summary: Proud Tek is a direct RFID factory in Shenzhen — operating since 2008 and shipping to B2B buyers worldwide — that works as a single-source RFID solution provider: we help you choose the chip, build the tag, card, label or wristband, pre-encode it with your data, and ship it read-verified with the compliance paperwork already attached. What we are not is a reader or middleware vendor; the deliverable is working, standards-based media plus the partner recommendations to run it, not a black box you can only refill through us. This page lays out the capability menu, the sample-to-PO path, and the certifications and QC records your procurement team can verify before the first order.
heroPoints: One partner across four product families — RFID cards and fobs, UHF inlays and labels, NFC tags and stickers, and event wristbands — plus the encoding, sampling and compliance work most trading companies quietly subcontract.
A direct factory, not a trading desk: production in Shenzhen under one ISO 9001 management system, with every encoded unit read-tested before it ships.

A qualifying path built for procurement — a free sample pack, a 100-piece pilot, then locked-price volume, with factory-audit access and verifiable ISO 9001 / 14001 / 45001 certificates at every step.

brief.label: What Proud Tek is
brief.text: A Shenzhen RFID factory, direct since 2008, that ships qualified tags, cards, labels and wristbands together with the encoding, sampling and compliance paperwork around them — one supplier, one management system, one point of accountability.

sections.title: What a full RFID solution provider actually delivers
sections.intro: 'Solution provider' is one of the most abused phrases in RFID sourcing — half the vendors using it are trading desks that drop-ship a catalogue. Proud Tek uses it in the literal sense: we own the steps between your requirement and your loading dock. That means selecting the chip and antenna, building the [RFID tag](/products/rfid-tags/) or [card](/products/rfid-cards/), pre-encoding it with your data, and folding the result into a program we can scale and schedule — including standing supply for [supply-chain and inventory rollouts](/solutions/rfid-supply-chain-management/). The numbers below are the ones a procurement team checks first.
bullets: Application consulting — we take your environment, read distance, throughput and budget and map them to a frequency (LF 125 kHz, HF 13.56 MHz or UHF 860-960 MHz), a chip and a form factor, rather than selling whatever is in stock.

Custom tag and card development — where a catalogue part will not do, our RF engineers design the antenna, choose the substrate and housing, and prototype against your real surface and duty cycle; typical custom development runs 4-8 weeks.

Encoding and data services — UID databases, NDEF records, MIFARE Classic sector-key and DESFire application setup, and GS1 EPC encoding, all written on the line and read-verified before packing (see the [card encoding service](/lp/rfid-card-encoding-service/)).
Pilot supply — 100 pcs to 1,000 pieces of the shortlisted options for side-by-side field testing, with read-range data returned so the decision is evidence-based, not a guess.
Volume production and supply management — once a spec is locked, we run it at volume with locked pricing, scheduled call-offs and a bonded-warehouse safety-stock program for repeat buyers.

sections.title: Where we stop — and who we hand off to
sections.intro: A page titled 'solution provider' should be honest about its edges, because the expensive surprises in RFID come from the gap between 'they said turnkey' and what actually shipped. Proud Tek owns the media and the data on it. We do not sell the readers, gateways or middleware — instead we spec them, name proven partners, and make sure the credential we ship drops straight into that stack. For the reader and encoding side of a deployment, our [readers and encoding solution page](/solutions/rfid-readers-and-encoding/) covers how the handoff works.

Integration support means encoding-format design, reader recommendations and pilot assistance — we bridge tag-to-system, not rewrite your software.
Custom means an engineered antenna, substrate and housing tuned to your surface and read distance — not just print.
A named account engineer owns the program through reorders, with 3-5 business day bonded call-offs for repeat volume.

sections.title: From free sample to standing PO
sections.intro: Nobody should commit a production budget to a tag they have not held. The path below is the one we actually run, and it is deliberately front-loaded with cheap, reversible steps: a [free sample pack](/sample-pack/) first, a small paid pilot second, and a locked-price production order only once the parts have earned it on your own bench.

image.alt: A five-step sourcing flow from left to right: a free sample pack of 8-12 SKUs shipping in 5-10 business days, a written spec and quote, a 100-piece pilot tested on the buyer's own readers, a first-article lock, then a locked-price volume PO with 100% read-back verification and 3-5 business day bonded call-offs.

faq.question: How do I verify your factory before placing an order?
faq.answer: Three independent checks. First, request our ISO 9001, ISO 14001 and ISO 45001 certificate numbers and confirm them directly with the issuing registrar. Second, book a factory audit — engineering and quality-system audits at our Shenzhen operation are by appointment, with virtual walk-throughs for buyers who cannot travel and third-party (TUV, SGS, Intertek) visits accommodated when your program requires them. Third, order a sample pack and put the parts on your own readers. Every claim on this page is meant to be checked, not taken on faith.

faq.question: What happens if the samples fail on our reader?
faq.answer: That is exactly what the sample and pilot stages are for. If a sample does not read reliably on your specified reader, we treat it as an engineering problem, not a lost sale: our RF team retunes the antenna, adjusts the chip or changes the substrate and re-samples. For access-control and hotel-lock formats we test the first article on the actual reader or lock hardware before the volume run, so a reader mismatch surfaces at sample stage — not at unit 40,000.

faq.question: What are your payment and MOQ terms for a first order?
faq.answer: Pilot quantities start at 100 pieces, so a first engagement stays low-risk. Production minimums and payment terms depend on the product family, chip allocation and encoding scheme — we quote them per program rather than post a single number that would be wrong for half of them. Send your spec and target volume and you will have written terms and pricing before anything is tooled or encoded.

faq.question: Can you help us choose between NFC and UHF for our project?
faq.answer: Yes — technology selection is the first thing our solutions team does. NFC at 13.56 MHz suits tap-to-read interactions with a smartphone, short-range access and product authentication; UHF at 860-960 MHz suits bulk scanning, longer read range and high-throughput inventory. We weigh your read distance, volume, environment and how the end user interacts with the tag, then recommend the frequency, chip and form factor — and prove it with a mixed sample pack you can test both ways.

faq.question: Do you actually sell complete RFID systems with readers and software?
faq.answer: No — and it is better for you that we are clear about it. Our deliverable is the tag, card, label or wristband and the data encoded on it. We provide reader recommendations, encoding-format design and pilot support, and we work alongside reader makers (Impinj, Zebra, Alien) and software platforms so the credential we ship integrates cleanly. If a vendor promises tags, readers, middleware and installation all from one warehouse, ask where each part is actually made.
